try_responsive_units_minmax_and_fluid_tr.title: Try it yourself: Let the main region use the available width
try_responsive_units_minmax_and_fluid_tr.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

The Grid has a readable maximum `width` from earlier work, but the main region still carries a narrower percentage `width`. A 100% fluid `width` lets it use the available space inside its containing context while later `max-width` rules can still cap it. Continue from the Grid checkpoint. Append `main { width: 100%; }`. Resize the preview: main should use the available `width` more fully without exceeding its broader layout constraints.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for let the main region use the available width so it reinforces Responsive Units, minmax(), and Fluid Tracks.

try_responsive_units_minmax_and_fluid_tr.title: Try it yourself: Create fluid Grid tracks with minmax()
try_responsive_units_minmax_and_fluid_tr.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

A fixed two-column Grid can squeeze items when the viewport becomes narrow. auto-fit with minmax() lets the browser choose how many useful tracks fit while preserving a practical minimum card `width`. Continue the cumulative stylesheet. Add `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(16rem, 1fr));` in a later `main` rule. Narrow and widen the preview: columns should collapse and expand automatically instead of staying locked at two.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for create fluid Grid tracks with minmax() so it reinforces Responsive Units, minmax(), and Fluid Tracks.

try_responsive_units_minmax_and_fluid_tr.title: Try it yourself: Cap the fluid layout at a readable width
try_responsive_units_minmax_and_fluid_tr.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

The fluid Grid can grow comfortably, but on very wide screens the whole reading area can become too broad. A rem-based maximum combined with automatic inline margins caps and centers the layout without giving up fluid behavior below the cap. Continue the cumulative stylesheet. Add `max-width: 72rem;` and `margin-inline: auto;` to a later `main` rule. Widen the preview: main should stop growing at a readable `width` and remain centered.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for cap the fluid layout at a readable width so it reinforces Responsive Units, minmax(), and Fluid Tracks.
